# Local changes to Servo selectors 0.38.0

Upstream: https://github.com/servo/stylo, revision `572ecba2d1600e7c3d490586692a209faf703baa`, `selectors` directory. The locked crates.io archive SHA-256 is `8adfa1c298912827b8a28b223b3b874357397ae706e6190acd9bf28cee99114d`. Source headers and the MPL-2.0 licence are retained.

The selected [CSS Nesting publication, 22 January 2026](https://www.w3.org/TR/2026/WD-css-nesting-1-20260122/#nest-selector), defines nesting specificity as the greatest specificity of the parent's complex selectors. Count generated pseudo-elements when computing that specificity. Upstream omitted their contribution while recomputing a nesting parent's flags and specificity. Their matching flags remain excluded from the child, and the parent pseudo-elements still cannot match through `&`.

The public `nesting_ampersand_lists_and_specificity` renderer regression distinguishes a parent list containing `.parent::before` from its `.parent` alternative, with a later rule that would otherwise win the incorrect specificity tie. No selector matcher, grammar or data table has been replaced.

Reuse cached specificity for generated pseudo-element parents after that correction. This avoids recursively recounting already-resolved ancestor selectors at every nesting level.

Expose defaulted parent-selector discovery/resolution hooks on implementation-owned pseudo-classes. The DOM adapter uses them for selector arguments of functional `:current()`, and its existing visitor traverses those arguments. Without these hooks, an `&` inside `:current()` was invisible to nesting, incorrectly adding an implicit descendant combinator to `:is(:current(&), p)`. The public regression requires that rule's `p` branch to retain its nonrelative matching behavior; no timeline state is fabricated.

Keep the selector builder on the heap and perform its allocation/finalization outside recursive parsing frames. Read functional pseudo-class tokens before entering their nested selector parser, so unrelated simple-selector parsing locals do not remain on the recursive stack. The supported component-depth boundary is exercised by parsing and matching 255 nested `:is()` functions on the normal library test thread; a composed nesting selector also matches at the inclusive resolved-depth limit. No test-thread stack override or lower resource limit is used.

Respect the existing `parse_host()` feature gate for functional `:host()` as well as plain `:host`. The DOM adapter now enables it together with native shadow matching, so capability queries accept both forms.

Add `:host-context()` to the native component AST, compound-argument parser, specificity builder, nesting substitution, visitor and matcher. Host arguments match in each candidate's normal containing tree, preventing `:host(:host)` and `:host-context(:host)` from retaining the declaring shadow host. Host-context traversal uses shadow-including ancestors. Host and slotted arguments expose their selector-list boundaries to the existing structural visitor. Parse host arguments in a shared helper outside the functional dispatch frame: duplicating their construction in that recursive dispatch exhausted the normal thread stack even for the existing 255-level `:is()` regression. The renderer additionally exercises both host functions at the inclusive component limit and rejects one further level with the existing typed error.

Expose the corresponding defaulted scope-selector discovery hook for custom selector arguments. The DOM's `:current()` implementation forwards its argument-list scope flags, so `:is(:current(:scope), p)` is nonrelative within a scope even though timeline state is inactive. A public regression observed the incorrect implicit descendant before this hook.

Add a default-false virtual-root query to the Element adapter. Ancestor traversal routes such a root through the existing featureless matching path. The DOM adapter supplies a distinct virtual document node only during document-scoped matching; it can anchor `:scope > html` but cannot be a selector subject or match an ordinary universal/type/attribute selector. Ordinary and element-scoped matching retain their existing tree boundaries. No alternative matcher is introduced.

Extend reverse part-name lookup with a defaulted multi-name hook, preserving existing adapters. Translate and deduplicate alternatives independently at each export boundary, then intersect requested part names on the subject element. This supports nested many-to-one exports without Cartesian expansion. A part combinator reaching the declaring shadow host preserves its featureless state.

Expose the existing host/slot origin traversal for stylesheet visibility and scope ancestry, so the DOM and style adapters reuse the native alias relation. Slotted arguments share the normal-context argument matcher with host selectors. Actual shadow slots remain transparent to flattened aliases; the DOM adapter supplies fallback alias links separately from real assigned-slot identity. Generated before/after pseudo-elements are accepted after slotted selectors by the adapter's existing validity hook.

Reset the compound-only combinator restriction when entering a nested selector list. Host and slotted arguments remain compounds, while `:is()`, `:not()`, `:has()` and `:nth-child(... of ...)` within those compounds retain their own complex-selector grammars. The renderer regression distinguishes valid nested complex selectors from still-invalid direct complex host/slotted arguments.

Enumerate every valid alias origin in the source context without allocation. Nested fallback slots can expose one subject through several slots in the same root; parts can originate on both a nested host and the declaring host itself. Match each origin using a restored temporary context value, and retain the exact origin through scope proximity, prefix matching and exported-name translation. This replaces the earlier singular-origin helper; ordinary selector matching keeps its direct path.
